defaultCommands.intro: Default commands come with the bot. You don't need to create them: you can turn them on or off one by one from Commands → Default in the dashboard. The description, aliases and examples on this page are the same ones you see in the dashboard.

microCommands.title: Micro commands
microCommands.subtitle: Chat shortcuts to change the stream category
microCommands.what: A micro command is a short command you choose, for example !apex, that switches the stream category to a game you assigned to it. Instead of typing !game Apex Legends, you type !apex.
how: You create the micro command and assign it a game or category.
The streamer or a moderator types the command in chat.
Decatron changes the stream category and replies with the category that was set.
microCommands.exampleCode:
AnthonyDeca: !g set !apex Apex Legends
Decatron: Micro command !apex created for: Apex Legends

Moderator: !apex
Decatron: Category changed to: Apex Legends! (using !apex)
microCommands.who: Only the streamer and the channel moderators. If anyone else types a micro command, the bot tells them they don't have permission.
panel: Type the command name without the “!” (for example: lol, cs, val). The prefix is added for you.
Search for the game and pick it from the list.
microCommands.panelNote: If you create a micro command with a name that already exists, it is updated with the new game. To change the game of an existing one use “Edit”: the command name can't be changed.
microCommands.chatIntro: The !g command shows and changes the category, and also manages micro commands. It is for the streamer and moderators only.
chatRows: Creates or updates the !apex micro command
rules: After the “!” only letters and numbers are allowed, with no spaces or symbols.
These names are reserved and can't be used: !g, !game, !set, !remove, !delete, !list, !help, !title and !t.
microCommands.panelAccess: To view, create and edit micro commands you need the “Commands” access level or higher. To delete them you need “Moderation” or higher.
req: The default command !game must be turned on in your channel (Commands → Default). If it is off, micro commands don't respond.
Today micro commands change the category on Twitch. On Kick, changing the category is coming soon, same as !game.
microCommands.counters: Micro commands don't count anything. For a counter (deaths, wins…) create a custom command with the $(count) variable.
